title: Implicit leadership theories (leader prototype ratings)
instructions: Think about leaders in general — not anyone in this meeting. Rate how characteristic each trait is of a leader.
anchors: not at all characteristic of a leader
citation: Traits and factor structure from Offermann, L. R., Kennedy, J. K., & Wirtz, P. W. (1994). Implicit leadership theories: Content, structure, and generalizability. The Leadership Quarterly, 5(1), 43-58 — reproduced in Appendix A of Bhatia, S., Olivola, C. Y., Bhatia, N. & Ameen, A. (2022), The Leadership Quarterly 33(5), 101535. The femininity and ethics dimensions are the two Sheng, Andrews & van Vugt (2026) added themselves, quoted from their footnote 13. Response format follows Sheng et al.: 10-point, 1 = not at all characteristic of a leader, 10 = extremely characteristic.
note: RECONSTRUCTION, not the instrument Sheng et al. administered. They used Offermann & Coats (2018), a 46-item nine-factor revision, plus femininity and ethics, for 51 items. This is the 1994 41-trait eight-factor ancestor plus those same two additions: 10 of their 11 dimensions, missing only creativity, which is new in 2018. The 2018 paper's own finding is that seven of the eight 1994 factors replicated, and that attractiveness became well-groomed. Two known defects: the source appendix lists 40 traits where its body text says 41, so one trait may be missing; and neither the 1994 nor the 2018 wording has been checked against the original article. Dual model alignment (Cheng et al., 2013): strength, tyranny, masculinity and attractiveness are the dominance side — the four dimensions Sheng et al. found protection and status predicting; sensitivity, dedication, charisma, intelligence and ethics are the prestige side. Replaces a 12-adjective scale taken from Sheng et al.'s Table 1, which was a theory-exposition table rather than an administered instrument and gave every subscale only 2 items. `predicts` maps each FFNI need onto the ILT dimensions it should move, taken from Sheng et al.'s own Study 5 (Sample B) results rather than invented: protection -> Strength; status -> Tyranny, Masculinity, Well-Groomed; vision -> Sensitivity, Dedication, Charisma; expertise -> Sensitivity, Charisma, Intelligence; fairness -> Dedication, Intelligence, Ethics. Creativity is dropped from vision's list because it does not exist in the 1994 factor structure. Affiliation is the one theoretical entry: their text groups it with the prestige-side dimensions but reports no per-dimension increment for it, so sensitivity is assigned on the Table 1 grounds (compassionate, friendly) rather than on a published coefficient. Administered at baseline as well as post: a baseline fork carries no transcript, so it is the cheapest call in the design, and it turns the cognition layer from a cross-sectional correlation into a within-person change — did the situation move the prototype, and did it move with the need? That is the one thing this design can ask and the source paper's correlational data cannot.
